question: How does Bokor connect a sustained melody above the piano’s broken chords?
intro: Judith Bokor’s Columbia side pairs cello with piano, whose player is not identified. The upstream discography dates matrix F 87 only to circa 1925; the exact day supplied on Commons is not established for this side.

sections.label: Middle expansion
sections.mNote: analysis landmark, not an aligned bar boundary

sections.label: Later melodic span
sections.mNote: a quieter passage precedes another recorded swell

cues.title: Melody above broken chords
cues.text: Bokor’s cello carries the long line above piano accompaniment. Follow the connection between sustained notes while the piano keeps renewing its sound; do not mistake the transfer’s surface noise for articulation.
cues.evidence: The upstream catalogue identifies cello with piano. The written texture is described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_cygne. This whole-performance suggestion makes no timed entrance or measured vibrato claim.

cues.title: An early rise and retreat
cues.text: The early span grows towards a crest and then relaxes. Compare the continuity of the melodic line across that rise with the changing weight beneath it.
cues.evidence: The report places boundaries at 0:32 and 0:44. Relative level rises from −19.9 dB at 0:25 to −10.3 dB at 0:40, then falls to −19.0 dB at 0:45; the analysis does not separate cello and piano.

cues.title: A crest before the pause
cues.text: Through the middle expansion, follow the phrase towards its stronger crest and the quieter space beyond it. The contrast belongs to this transfer’s recorded contour, not a measurement of the cellist’s bow pressure.
cues.evidence: The 1:10 and 1:20 windows are among the report’s highest; a boundary at 1:26 precedes the low 1:30 window. No bowing technique is inferred from relative level.

cues.title: The later swell
cues.text: After the quieter passage, the line gathers weight again. Hear the later swell as a complete ascent and release, keeping the piano’s movement in view as well as the cello.
cues.evidence: Relative level rises from −24.5 dB at 1:30 to −8.2 dB at 1:50, then falls to −15.2 dB at 2:00. Instrument roles are documented; the analysis measures the combined sound.

cues.title: Releasing the last phrase
cues.text: The final passage withdraws, leaving less melodic sound against the surviving surface noise. Listen through the release rather than treating the end of the phrase as a sudden silence.
cues.evidence: The 2:18 boundary lies in the withdrawal; relative level falls to −28.6 dB at 2:25 and −41.1 dB at 2:30. High detected onset counts are not interpreted as performed notes in this noisy transfer.

transitions.title: The phrase gains weight
transitions.how: The cello-and-piano texture continues while the phrase builds towards a stronger crest. The section marker follows a measured change inside that continuous texture, not a new instrument entrance.
transitions.evidence: The 0:58 boundary precedes the rising level towards 1:10–1:20. Exact bars and bow strokes are not identified.

transitions.title: A crest opens into quieter space
transitions.how: The middle swell gives way to a quieter passage before the next ascent. The cello and piano remain the same forces; changing phrase weight supplies the contrast.
transitions.evidence: Boundary at 1:26; relative level falls from −8.2 dB at 1:20 to −24.5 dB at 1:30.

transitions.title: The final phrase loses weight
transitions.how: The later swell recedes into the closing phrase. Attend to the sustained line as the recording becomes quieter, then to the remaining resonance and surface sound.
transitions.evidence: Boundaries at 2:10 and 2:18; level falls substantially in the 2:15–2:30 span. No exact final note is claimed.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.note: Rule 3: the upstream catalogue identifies this historical Columbia D 9758/F 87 issue as circa 1925, establishing publication before 1963. Its European 50-year recording term expired before the 2013 extension. Exact first-publication year at the US cutoff is not independently established, and US public-domain status is not asserted. Opened IA metadata has no licenseurl and no non-commercial licence. The Commons composition-only tags are not the acceptance basis.
